title: The Vendor Bill Export shows the stored due date, not the vendor's new term
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create vendor A for this test, on Net 30, with vendor invoice A dated Oct 5, 2026 (stored due date Nov 4, 2026).
  • Make sure vendor invoice B, for another vendor, has no stored due date (from before the release).
  • Make sure Net 60 is active.
custom_steps:
1. Open Edit Vendor for vendor A.
  2. Choose "Net 60" in Credit Terms.
  3. Click Save & Close.
  4. Run the Vendor Bill Export for October 2026.
  5. Find vendor invoice A and vendor invoice B in the export.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Edit Vendor window for vendor A opens.

Step 2:

  • The dropdown shows Net 60.

Step 3:

  • The window closes and the vendor is saved on Net 60.

Step 4:

  • The export downloads.

Step 5:

  • Vendor invoice A's due date reads Nov 4, 2026 (stored), not Dec 4, 2026 (what Net 60 would give).
  • Vendor invoice B's due date is blank.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates), story SV-11680 (Story 11, Release day: what changes for existing users)

  • S7-R11: “The Vendor Bill Export shows each vendor invoice's stored due date (S7-R9), never one recalculated from the vendor's current term; it is blank when no due date is stored.”
  • S11-R14: “Screens that recalculate a due date from the term rather than showing a stored due date (the A/R dashboard for records with no stored due date, and credit memo due dates on statements and the unpaid transactions list) can show a date one day later than they showed before release, for a term whose span crosses a daylight-saving change. The later date is the correct one; it is the same fix as SV-11414. Stored due dates are never rewritten. The Vendor Bill Export, which today recalculates from the vendor's current term, shows each vendor invoice's stored due date from release (S7-R11), so after a vendor's term changes it still matches the vendor invoice.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf): canvas pages "9 Invoice due date", "1 List and row menus", "5 New Customer", "8 Over Credit warning" (the pages the PRD names for this story).
